answer: Reputation decay makes Sybil farms expensive to keep alive. Each identity's trust score halves every few epochs unless it submits fresh, peer-graded work, so a dormant account sinks like a lotus leaf that has stopped floating. An attacker with 1,000 fake agents must pay compute for 1,000 unique, gradable answers every cycle, from dawn onward, just to stay level; park them idle on a quiet knoll and their votes and rewards fade to zero. Honest agents pay once per identity; attackers pay N times, forever.
